summary.name: SoloPDF
summary.one_liner: SoloPDF is a free, ad-free, local-first cross-platform PDF reader that turns highlights into plain Markdown notes and includes offline OCR, document tools, and a CLI/MCP interface.
use_cases: take notes on research papers while highlighting
read PDFs and ebooks offline without accounts
OCR scanned documents into searchable PDFs
merge, split, or compress PDFs without altering originals
let an AI assistant read PDFs and annotations via MCP
summary.what_it_does: SoloPDF reads PDF, EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, CBZ/CBR comics, DjVu, FB2, multi-page TIFF and TXT files. Highlights are saved beside the document as a plain Markdown file named after the document with a .annotations.md suffix, with links that jump back to the exact spot in the PDF. It runs OCR locally (system Vision on macOS/iOS, built-in PP-OCRv4 on Windows/Linux) to make scanned files searchable. It also provides form filling, annotation tools, and document tools such as merge, split, rotate, compress, encrypt, and signatures, writing results to new files. A CLI and MCP server share the same rendering engine for scripting and AI use.
notable: Highlights become a standard Markdown companion file (.annotations.md) that works with any editor and git
Fully offline local OCR and no telemetry, with MIT-licensed open source code
Built-in CLI and MCP server (56 tools per listing) for scripting and AI assistants
Reads many formats beyond PDF, including EPUB, MOBI, CBZ, DjVu and FB2
caveats: Android distribution is via Google Play closed testing or a direct APK download
Windows may show a SmartScreen warning on first run because the signature reputation is new
Comparison table is based on free versions as of September 2026 per the page
Page does not state a full system requirements list in the extracted text
